title: Hokule‘a 1980 (reprinted in “A Journey by the Stars”)
authors: Will Kyselka; introduced by Cecil Heftel
locator: Congressional Record, 17 September 1980, Extensions of Remarks, p. 25908; original Ka ‘Elele, July 1980. Only the Kyselka item and introduction inspected, not unrelated remarks.
scope_limit: Participant account, not independent performance audit. The congressional introduction oversimplifies navigation as entirely by stars; the reproduced account describes several cues, planetarium training, escort communication and comparison with instrument fixes.
evidence_lineage: Contemporaneous participant account republished verbatim from the Bishop Museum newsletter; congressional republication is not independent corroboration. Raw fix logs and original newsletter not acquired.

title: History: The Story of Hōkūle‘a
locator: Sections The Story of Hōkūle‘a, first voyage, tragedy, A Generation of Renewal, Master Navigators.
scope_limit: Community institution’s retrospective public history; commemorative claims about whole-population identity, last voyages and causal effects on all Hawaiian culture are not adopted here.
evidence_lineage: PVS participant memories and institutional narrative; overlaps the same voyages and network as S01 and S03. Exact archival bases of every statement not supplied.

title: Hōkūleʻa Mo‘olelo: The Pwo Ceremony
locator: 17 March 2017 post; first-person account of March 2007 Satawal visit and initiation; final adaptation note.
scope_limit: Eyewitness ceremony account adapted a decade later from Hawaiki Rising. Use March 2007 rather than exact ceremony day because S02 gives 18 March and this post gives 17 March. Heroic claims and unrelated political chronology are not used.
evidence_lineage: Sam Low’s witnessed ceremony and his own book, republished by PVS. S02 and S03 are one institutional lineage, not independent evidence for broader cultural impact.

title: Dating Aboriginal stone-walled fishtraps at Lake Condah, southeast Australia
authors: Gunditj Mirring Traditional Owners Aboriginal Corporation
locator: Journal of Archaeological Science 39:268–286; article text inspected via https://www.academia.edu/16379574/Dating_Aboriginal_stone_walled_fishtraps_at_Lake_Condah_southeast_Australia ; especially pp.268–272, 279–284, sections 3.9 and 4.
scope_limit: HTML extraction of article sections, not downloaded publisher PDF. Sediment-charcoal ages and stratigraphy constrain one feature’s history; stone itself was not radiocarbon dated; no regional adoption rate.
evidence_lineage: Original partnership excavations at Muldoons Trap Complex, channel F10, sediment analyses and 16 AMS dates; later nomination S05 inherits this chronology rather than independently reproducing it.

title: Budj Bim Cultural Landscape: World Heritage Nomination
authors: Commonwealth of Australia, Department of the Environment and Energy; developed with Gunditjmara Traditional Owners
locator: December 2017 dossier: front matter; Part 2B, especially pp.68–70 on drainage and restoration; pp.18–21 and 36–40 on system and chronology. Selected sections inspected.
scope_limit: Nomination is a selective argument for heritage recognition. Colonial observations and older scholarship are mediated citations unless separately inspected. Use local engineered-water outcomes, not oldest/continuous/universal welfare superlatives.
evidence_lineage: Combines Gunditjmara testimony and custodial knowledge, archaeological work including S04, earlier histories and restoration feasibility/management records. The latter reports were referenced but not independently acquired; shares community project lineage with S06.

title: Lake Condah Restoration Project
authors: Gunditj Mirring Traditional Owners Aboriginal Corporation
locator: Project page, paragraphs on 1954 drain, failed trial, 2004 plan, 2006 studies, March 2008 return and January–May 2010 construction; employment bullets.
scope_limit: Direct implementing institution’s account, not independent labour evaluation. No worker count, wage series, retention or household income distribution. Page undated; inspected 5 November 2026.
evidence_lineage: Gunditj Mirring account of its restoration programme and partners, including funding, tendering and training; substantially same project history reused in S05.

title: The “fire stick farming” hypothesis: Australian Aboriginal foraging strategies, biodiversity, and anthropogenic fire mosaics
locator: PNAS 105:14796–14801; PDF https://web.stanford.edu/~jhj1/papers/bird_etal2008.pdf ; Ethnoecological Context, three Results tests, Discussion, Materials and Methods.
scope_limit: Observed contemporary Martu hunts and landscape comparisons, not randomized burning assignments; broad ancient-Australia claims exceed study. Species diversity is not identical to successional patch diversity.
evidence_lineage: Original 2002 field observations (1,095 forager-hours, 421 bouts, 59 camp-days), 34 landscape circles and Landsat classification; some hunting results reprise team’s previous field publications. Overlaps study programme and population with S08.

title: Aboriginal hunting buffers climate-driven fire-size variability in Australia’s spinifex grasslands
locator: PNAS 109:10287–10292; Results, Tables 1–2, Discussion, Materials and Methods.
scope_limit: Regimes classified by proximity to communities/tracks, not ignition observation of every fire; nonrandom spatial comparison; contemporary regional study. Mammal-population benefit is proposed, not directly measured here.
evidence_lineage: Original 1999–2010 Landsat sequence and 2000–2010 foraging observations (347 sample days, 1,811 bouts, 104 foragers); extends and partly overlaps S07, rather than independent replication.

title: Origins of Agriculture at Kuk Swamp in the Highlands of New Guinea
locator: Science 301:189–193; acquired https://faculty.washington.edu/plape/pacificarchaut12/Denham%20et%20al%202003.pdf ; Site and stratigraphy, Archaeological evidence, Table 1.
scope_limit: Original article acquired; supporting online material not separately inspected. Cultivation inference combines proxies. Earliest phase and global independent-invention conclusion require more evidence than the dates alone.
evidence_lineage: Renewed Kuk excavations, sediment sequence, radiocarbon dates, pollen/phytolith/starch and other proxies, interpreting earlier Kuk research. S10 revisits shared site and evidence, not a fully independent confirmation.

title: Phase 3: The Emergence of Ditches
locator: In Ten Thousand Years of Cultivation at Kuk Swamp, Terra Australis 46, pp.221–237, DOI 10.22459/TA46.07.2017.13; especially pp.224–225, 234–237.
scope_limit: Kuk is better investigated than comparator valleys; reconstructions of property, risk and causes of abandonment are explicit hypotheses, not recovered institutions or recorded decisions.
evidence_lineage: Excavation records and ditch plans from Kuk, with published records from Warrawau, Kana, Tambul and Haeapugua. Shared Kuk lineage with S09; some other-site evidence is mediated through earlier reports.

title: Experimental Growing of Pre-European Cultivars of Kūmara (Sweet Potato, Ipomoea batatas [L.] Lam.) at the Southern Margins of Māori Horticulture
locator: NZ Journal of Archaeology 23 (2001), published 2003, pp.161–188; text inspected via https://www.academia.edu/111593238/Experimental_growing_of_pre_European_cultivators_of_kumara_sweet_potato_Ipomoea_Batatas_L_Lam_at_the_southern_margins_of_Maori_horticulture ; pp.162–173,177–185.
scope_limit: Initial NZAA parameterized PDF redirected to an unrelated fishing paper; rejected and documented. Correct article verified by title, authors and page footer in HTML mirror. Modern climate, virus-treated collection stock, fencing/windbreak and unreplicated plots; traditional storage not replicated.
evidence_lineage: Original gardens at Robin Hood Bay and Whatarangi, starting 1999/2000; inherited cultivar collection assembled by Yen in 1955–1958 and later repatriated and treated. Cultivar authenticity assessed morphologically, not proof of unchanged ancient yield potential.

title: Research at the interface between Indigenous knowledge and soil science; weaving knowledges to understand horticultural land use in Aotearoa / New Zealand
scope_limit: Pōhatu site and two soil profiles; specific amendment identifications and temporal interpretations remain uncertain. Research supports restoration goals but does not establish a new garden’s adoption, commercial viability or employment effects.
evidence_lineage: Original collaborative soil investigation and Mana Whenua interpretation; place names, waiata and manuscripts mediated partly through coauthor Payne’s 2020 research; contemporary geochemistry and microbotany. Historical deed narrative cites Evison, not inspected original deed.

title: American sweet potato and Asia-Pacific crop experimentation during early colonisation of temperate-climate Aotearoa/New Zealand
locator: Antiquity 98(401):1376–1394; Cambridge HTML and PDF extraction, especially Results, Table 1/Figure 10 and Discussion pp.1383–1391; https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/antiquity/article/american-sweet-potato-and-asiapacific-crop-experimentation-during-early-colonisation-of-temperateclimate-aotearoanew-zealand/B6446CB196635B1CDB44DC7506F696C8 .
scope_limit: Article text inspected; supplementary reference granule atlas and full model not independently reanalysed. Morphological starch assignments are probabilistic; absence of taro/yam in later samples does not prove cultural disappearance across Te Waipounamu.
evidence_lineage: New starch/palynomorph analysis and radiocarbon modelling at M24/11 using earlier excavation contexts; some site interpretation inherits Barber’s prior reports. Separate material from Pōhatu and Cook Strait trials.

title: He Pukoa Kani ‘Āina: Kanaka Maoli approaches to mo‘okū‘auhau as methodology
locator: AlterNative 8(2):137–147; PDF text inspected, especially pp.142–145 on interviews, volunteering, Shantell Ching and other women’s accounts. Filename ends 143 but article continues to 147.
scope_limit: Methodological article excerpting purposive interviews and researcher experience; not representative survey, wage study or proof of supernatural/biological mechanisms. Accounted beliefs are evidence of meaning, not independently verified physical explanations.
evidence_lineage: Author’s original interviews and participant experience, drawing on her 2010 doctoral thesis. This is a distinct research collection, while interviewees belong to the same voyaging network as S01–S03; full thesis not inspected.
